title: Why Diesel Engines Skip Spark Plugs

segments.text: Can a car run without a spark plug?
A diesel engine ignites fuel by compressing air.
The piston compresses air, raising its temperature enough to ignite the injected diesel fuel.
When diesel is sprayed into that hot air, it ignites instantly.
This method powers massive ships and heavy trucks.
Torque comes from how much fuel you inject, not from throttling air.
The engine is designed to run on diesel fuel injected as a fine spray.
So the spark‑free surprise fuels the world because diesel engines skip spark plugs.
